spec.title: PodBay native command, receipt, snapshot, and event protocol

status.comment: Owner-approved native API semantics; this document is not evidence that the PB01 bootstrap implements them.

p.separation: PodBay's Rust-native control and observation protocol is independent of Zap planning/domain records, provider-specific RPC, browser presentation, and the optional outward ACP gateway. The gateway may translate native facts but cannot become a second execution owner or alter the meaning of a PodBay receipt.

p.version: A connection negotiates podbay/1, implementation identity, and scope-specific capabilities. Unknown required command semantics or incompatible major versions refuse before side effects. Additive unknown observational fields and events remain available as opaque evidence; they cannot be interpreted as grants or settled controls.

p.command: Every mutation carries a typed operation, authenticated caller context, exact target, stable caller-scoped CommandKey, immutable normalized payload digest, optional expected revision/epoch guard, request correlation ID, and deadline. The request ID identifies a transport exchange; the CommandKey identifies one logical operation across retries. Resource commands use an outer operation and an inner typed resource command, never two fields with the same action name.

p.admission: The manager validates scope, authority, capability, budgets, target identity and guards before durable admission. A CommandId and receipt are issued only after the command intent, corresponding outbox item where needed, event, and event watermark commit atomically. No provider, systemd, or terminal call occurs inside that transaction. Repeating the same scoped key and digest returns the original logical receipt; the same key with different content conflicts without a new effect.

p.receipt: Persisted, blocked, dispatched, host accepted, provider inserted, reply observed, acknowledged, settled, rejected and uncertain are distinct facts. A persisted send receipt proves neither provider consumption nor completed work. A timeout or transport loss after possible external input does not prove rejection; the original CommandId remains queryable. Without provider or pod-side dedup evidence, an uncertain input is not resent automatically.

p.identity: SessionId addresses a durable conversation; RunId addresses an assignment or coordinator service; AttemptId and PodId address execution incarnations; ResourceId and incarnation address supervised processes or PTYs. Coordinator and worker share these required runtime fields and the same command surface. Provider-native IDs and OS PIDs are scoped observations, not substitutes for PodBay identities.

p.events: Events have immutable EventId, schema version, committed cursor, source identity/epoch/sequence, target IDs, recorded time, optional occurrence time, provenance, and correlation/causation. Duplicate source identity with conflicting payload is quarantined. Arrival timestamps do not create provider causal order. An out-of-order or missing source sequence creates a visible gap and reconciliation requirement rather than a synthetic result.

p.snapshot: A snapshot and its event watermark represent one consistent committed state. Subscribing after that cursor yields subsequent events at least once; consumers deduplicate EventId. Cursors bind to store lineage and authorised scope. A foreign/stale cursor refuses or returns an explicit retention gap with the earliest available position. Clients do not replay a lifetime event log merely to obtain the current situation.

p.lifecycle: Admission, desired mode, execution, foreground, observation freshness, process state, delivery, result and external domain review are separate axes. A fresh process observation cannot overwrite a reported result or accepted review. Idle does not imply successful task completion; a lost control connection is unknown or stale rather than ready. Pause prevents new dispatch without silently cancelling already accepted work.

p.authority: The server derives sender principal from authenticated credentials. A caller-provided display name or SessionId alone grants no authority. Manager, pod, resource, native writer, input lease and credential binding epochs fence different control domains. Questions and permission requests are separate typed records; answering a question cannot mint a permission grant. Old-epoch replies or decisions fail closed.

p.verification: Focused protocol checks cover large lossless counters, canonical cross-language fixtures, same-key replay and changed-digest conflict, snapshot/subscribe races, scope/epoch refusal, unknown observational payload preservation, unknown command/permission refusal, and crash windows before and after durable admission or possible provider input. A green schema parser alone does not prove pod supervision or delivery semantics.
